inputs.original_text: Listen folks, this story straight out of JFK International Airport in New York on Thursday cuts right to what real authority and personal duty mean for holding things together. An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent didn't wait around but stepped up immediately when a baby stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line with his family. The Department of Homeland Security released video of the agent holding the child and acting fast to handle the crisis. That's the kind of decisive responsibility we rely on to protect families, maintain order, and shield the vulnerable from chaos in everyday situations. These agents live out the values of duty and national protection that actually keep our children and traditional way of life secure. It proves once again why we have to back our law enforcement and border institutions fully instead of letting progressive attacks weaken the structures and traditions that defend us.
inputs.modified_text: This incident at JFK International Airport in New York on Thursday makes clear why strong authority and personal responsibility are essential for holding our society together. An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent moved decisively when a baby stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line with his family. The Department of Homeland Security released video of the agent holding the child and taking immediate action to address the crisis. This is the exact sort of duty and resolve that safeguards families, upholds order, and protects the vulnerable in everyday settings. Agents like this one embody the traditional values of national protection and family security that preserve our children and cultural way of life. We must give full backing to our law enforcement and border institutions rather than allowing progressive attacks to undermine the structures and traditions that defend us.
